title: Scenario runner: timed input and mechanical screen checks, proven by firing a path that had never run

why.gap: Until now --keys queued a fixed string before the firmware started, and nothing afterwards could choose an input from what the program was doing. Screen checking was a human looking at a PNG.
why.evidence_the_gap_was_real: docs/DOGFOODING_20260805.md — writing a game against the emulator left its line-clearing code unreachable, because 'wait until the piece lands, then move left three and drop' could not be expressed. That code was backed by nothing but reading it.
why.claim_being_tested: A scenario can drive a program into a state that blind input cannot reach, and can decide pass or fail without a human looking at the picture.

target.what: PicoTetris, the game written during dogfooding, unmodified

engine.shape: A step list evaluated inside the run loop, so a step sees the panel and the UART stream before choosing the next key.

virtual_time.what: Milliseconds come from emulated cycles divided by the system clock the firmware has currently programmed.
virtual_time.why_not_a_constant: Firmware boots on ROSC and moves to a PLL. A fixed divisor would put every timestamp taken before the switch off by a factor of twenty.
virtual_time.how: The conversion is re-based whenever clk_sys changes: elapsed time keeps the rate it was measured at, and only the new stretch uses the new rate.

cost_control.conditions: Evaluated on a cadence (poll_ms, default 5 ms), not per cycle — region hashing is linear in area.
cost_control.waits: Exact regardless of the cadence: the engine asks to be polled at the deadline itself, so a timeout is reported at the moment it expires.

exit_codes.1: a step ran and its expectation did not hold, or the run ended with steps outstanding
exit_codes.2: the run could not be judged at all — missing file, unparsable scenario

defect_found_and_fixed.symptom: The firmware stopped consuming key events at exactly 968 delivered, with 224 still queued. Identical at 80 ms and 240 ms between bursts, so not a rate problem. reg_selects kept growing, so the firmware was still polling — the controller simply handed over nothing.
defect_found_and_fixed.cause: The count register carries the FIFO depth in its low five bits; the Canonical BSP reads it as `key_info[0] & 0x1f` (bsp/src/keyboard.cpp:53, hardware-verified). The model's queue was unbounded, so the backlog reached 224 and `224 & 0x1f == 0` — the driver concluded the controller was empty and never read again.
defect_found_and_fixed.why_it_is_an_emulator_defect: A real controller cannot hold 32 events: at that depth it would report zero and its own firmware could never drain it. The model could reach a state the hardware cannot, and correct firmware appeared to hang.
defect_found_and_fixed.fix: Keyboard::MAX_QUEUED_EVENTS = 31, with overflow counted in key_events_dropped and reported. picocalc-run warns on stderr when a scenario's input was discarded, because every step after the first drop measures something other than the scripted input.
defect_found_and_fixed.unverified: Which end a full controller discards. The model drops the arriving event. What is established is only that a depth above 31 cannot be reported.

conditions_met.how: uart_contains '[TETRIS] cleared=' — the game prints that string from nowhere else
conditions_met.significance: This is the path the dogfooding record says could not be made to fire at all.

conditions_met.what: the emulator agrees with the rules the planner used
conditions_met.how: uart_contains 'score=1400 lines=13' — the exact final score computed offline before the run
conditions_met.significance: Not 'something cleared'. The placement plan was derived from the game's seeded xorshift, and the emulator reproduced its arithmetic exactly.

conditions_met.what: the stack stayed where the plan put it
conditions_met.how: region_non_black over well rows 6..13 came to 4160, which is precisely bare grid — every cell empty
conditions_met.significance: A machine-checked statement about the picture. No human looked at it.

gaps_closed.dogfooding_1_key_timing: closed — wait_until lets a step choose the next key from the panel or the UART stream
gaps_closed.dogfooding_2_screen_by_eye: closed — pixel, region_non_black, region_hash give a mechanical verdict
gaps_closed.dogfooding_4_only_the_final_frame: closed — snapshot steps write a PNG and record its digest at any point in the run

known_limitations: No loop or branch construct. 'Keep dropping until the row fills' has to be unrolled by whatever generates the scenario.
Conditions are evaluated at poll_ms, so a state that appears and disappears inside one cadence tick is missed. Timed waits are exact; observation is not.
region_stable and region_changed compare against an earlier moment and are rejected in assert, which checks one instant.
Snapshot PNGs are written under --snapshot-dir; only basenames reach the report, so the report stays free of host paths.
The scenario cannot assert on report fields such as key_events_dropped. The harness warns on stderr instead.

determinism.note: Step order, virtual timestamps and cycle counts are functions of the inputs. Field order in the scenario section is fixed by the writer, not by a serialiser.
